- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model shows strong upward trend, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” rule: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike if sentiment remains neutral or bearish.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply a “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment drops below 0.50 within 3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending sharply, apply a “sentiment-weighted dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day if sentiment remains flat or declines.
